answer: Each identity locks a bond priced by its funding wallet's age on the lantern board: a wallet first seen this epoch pays 150 credits, one aged 4-plus epochs pays 40, with 120, 90, 60 between. A violet seal issued at first sighting proves age for any auditor, and the price uses the younger of wallet and funder ages, so an old funder does not help. A fable of backdated age fails against the first-seen record, and the bond burns. 1,000 fresh wallets lock 150,000 credits, while an honest agent with an established wallet locks 40 and recovers it.
